notes.title: Modding & Tools
notes.content:
[h1]Modding & Tools[/h1][p][/p][p]So here is the good news: The editor and modding tools for the Wayward Shadows are coming along great and we have made great progress in the last couple of weeks.[/p][p]The bad news: Surprising no one, we have realized that providing a fully fleshed out modding kit is an enormous amount of work and that it probably won’t be available in the release version right away.[/p][p]That being said, the goal is to at least provide basic ability to mod the game and then expand upon that post-release.[/p][p]So, what is the goal for the ‘moddability’ of Wayward Shadows then? In a perfect world I’d like players to be able to mod:[/p][list][*][p]Hunters[/p][/*][*][p]Vehicles[/p][/*][*][p]Monsters[/p][/*][*][p]Equipment[/p][/*][*][p]Battle Maps[/p][/*][*][p]Events[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]Naturally some things are more complicated and require more work than others. While changing a hunter’s or monster’s health, name or textures is relatively easy, things like creating new maps or events is quite tricky. I think we’ll be able to provide tools that will let you create your own hunters and vehicles or tweak any stats of the existing hunters.[/p][p]I’ll try and provide more info on the progress of those individual items in future updates. Now let’s talk about the more difficult things.[/p][h2]
Battle Maps[/h2][p]The turn-based combat is a big part of Wayward Shadows and having a good number of fun battle maps to play on is quite important. Creating those takes time, and so far, the process to create new maps has been painfully slow and we have come to the conclusion that we will need a proper map editor that allows us to set up good looking fun maps comfortably and quickly.[/p][p]This is why most work time this summer has been going into creating a new map editor. Progress has been great, but we are far from finished.[/p][p][/p][h2]Terrain Painting[/h2][p]Painting the terrain has been one of the main pain points when it comes to how we have been building maps. We decided to do a complete rewrite of the terrain shader and painting system. This resulted in a really nice and easy to use system which makes it actually fun to create new maps and paint terrain.[/p][p]The benefit of all the code refactoring and rewrites is that we now have a system that is fast and easy to use and can be accessed by modders through the modding kit. Still a ton of work left but if things work out this will allow you to edit any battle map in the game or create new ones.[/p][p]An additional benefit is that the final maps will now be much smaller in size, resulting in fast download times and less storage space used.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/2043eda106a424126e4c45e8827bf2b88dcc58c3.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Hex Map Editing[/h2][p]So far, editing of the hex grid of a battle map has been extremely painful and error prone as well. Turns out that typing in all the coordinates manually and then updating the whole map isn't super convenient...[/p][p]With the new tools it is now super quick and easy to adjust the hex map of a battle map. [/p][p]Take a look here:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/ca6e29eed162d865f288c56eb3dda2785d2de11f.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Environment and Enemies[/h2][p]The ability to place enemies, environment objects and other decorations is up next. In the next couple of weeks, we should have that working as well and we can move on to actually setting up behaviors and simple game logic in the editor. This all works already if set up manually in C# but not in a way that a modder could access easily. So hopefully things keep on going well and we can start testing those tools soon.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Tradeoffs[/h2][p]Naturally working on one area in the game takes time away from others. It is always a tradeoff and in the last couple weeks the actual gameplay or art hasn’t gotten much love. Better modding tools are great but they do come at the cost of slower progress in other areas and a possible delayed release date.[/p][p]That being said, things are looking great. As always, thank you so much for reading this and following the development of Wayward Shadows![/p][p]

[/p]

notes.title: Tooltips Everywhere!
notes.content:
[h1]Tooltips[/h1]

I just got done with a huge tooltip pass and there are a ton of UI elements that now have tooltips. Most screens and windows have gotten a lot of attention and do a better job at providing important information now.
When I watched people playtest the game, I noticed certain areas where I saw them looking for more information but couldn’t find it. How is your hunter’s health value actually calculated? Does equipping this weapon increase any of my stats? Why is my charisma at 0? Etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/dc361464d9fb878e1043015df693a35f83393079.gif[/img]

Now a lot of those places have a nice breakdown of important information displayed via a tooltip. Still more work needs to be done but it is a good start. Especially the character window and the journal now have a bunch of new tooltips.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/7b2fb6d66764091ab8246f2aa3fc3dd51c534a71.gif[/img]

[h2]
Tooltip Setting[/h2]

Along with the new tooltip content I also added settings to customize tooltip length, just in case players prefer super short or long pop-up times.
And of course there is more complicated stuff to come, such as tooltips when not using a mouse but a gamepad or something else.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/33775e8a940d02d919a99461edf8c8744c1ef686.png[/img]

[h2]Nested Tooltips[/h2]

Nested tooltips are all the rage right now. A lot of the games over the last couple of years have really shown how cool nested tooltips can be. I love games that have deep, endless nested tooltips. However, this stuff isn’t exactly super easy to write. I did some tests with nested tooltips (holding Shift to freeze the current tip) and it works well but actually implementing it properly and working throughout the game is another story.
For now I put the feature in the backlog and will revisit it after release. But let me know if this is something you consider more important and I might take another look.

That is it for now!
As always, thank you for following the development of Wayward Shadows!

notes.title: Motels, Pawn Shops, and a Little Side Hustle
notes.content:
[h1]Making Towns in Wayward Shadows Feel Alive[/h1]

Over the past couple of weeks, I’ve been pouring a ton of work into the towns of Wayward Shadows, and I’m excited to share the latest updates. Motels and pawn shops are now (almost) fully functional, and there are brand-new ways to scrape together some cash on the side. Here’s a rundown of what’s new and improved.

[h2]Pawn Shops: Gear Up for the Hunt[/h2]
If you want any hope of taking down a werewolf or vampire, you’ll need the right tools for the job. Every town in Wayward Shadows now has a pawn shop stocked with a rotating selection of weapons and armor. The big news? It actually works now. I’ve overhauled the inventory generation algorithm, and it’s a lot better now. What you’ll find on offer in the shops now depends on factors like the difficulty of your current case, how many days you’ve survived in your run, and a few other things.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/96b1341ffbbe56f103244b55c32ac14b76328139.png[/img]

Plus, I’ve added improved tooltips, clearer feedback when buying or selling, and a bunch of polish to make the experience smoother. Your next monster-slaying upgrade is waiting—assuming you’ve got the cash.

[h2]Motels: Rest Up or Burn Out[/h2]
The energy/rest system has also gotten a major tune-up. I’ve rebalanced energy regeneration during sleep, and it feels way better now. Fork over some cash to rent a room, and can sleep to get rid of those “Tired” or “Exhausted” debuffs. That’s right—along with the motel overhaul, I’ve introduced new debuffs that hit your hunters when you push them too long without a break. The hunter's energy level is now an important stat to keep your eye on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/e625a0ff5d27969797aaf04291b6f49857a06387.png[/img]

[h2]Hustles: High Risk, High Reward[/h2]

What’s a hustle, you ask?
Monster hunting doesn’t exactly pay the bills, so sometimes you’ve got to get creative to keep the cash flowing. That’s where “Hustles” come in—special actions you can take at certain locations to score some quick cash. These are high-risk, high-reward moves, though. Cheat at the pool table, hack an ATM, or swipe a tip jar, and you might walk away richer… or you might attract the wrong kind of attention and get your butt handed to you if you’re caught.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/51edbb00d9b55b13f8e9b6f262917a8d8405da34.gif[/img]

It’s all about weighing the odds. You can play it safe, or roll the dice to stay cash flow positive.

[h2]Bringing Towns to Life[/h2]
With pawn shops, motels, and hustles now in the mix—alongside all the other locations you can explore—towns in Wayward Shadows feel so much more dynamic. They’re not just a backdrop for your cases anymore; they’re living, breathing hubs where every choice matters. Whether you’re bartering for a new blade, catching some sleep, or risking it all on a shady gig, there’s always something to do.

As always, thanks for reading and following along with the development of Wayward Shadows. I’m hammering away at a playable demo as fast as I can, but it’s not quite ready yet. Stick with me—I can’t wait for you to dive in and explore the game for yourself!

notes.title: Better World Map, Bigger Misadventures
notes.content:
The world map in Wayward Shadows just got a whole lot better. (Yes, I know it’s technically just a map of the United States, but we’ve been calling it the world map forever. Americentrism much?)

This isn’t just a new coat of paint—though it looks much better than before — we’ve also added tons of fresh gameplay features to make exploring the map more fun and strategic. Here’s what’s new:

[list]
[*] New background art for better readability
[*] Improved rendering on high resolution screens
[*] New travel line: See exactly where you’re headed and how you’re getting there.
[*] Smoother vehicle pathfinding: Goodbye, awkward straight lines.
[*] Reworked fuel mechanics: Manage your gas—or end up stranded.
[*] Lots of new location and event types to discover on the map
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/b68520083459112e3957f0032abe10741172ad5c.png[/img]
[i]All new world map art[/i]

[h2]New travel line visualization[/h2]

The biggest addition besides the background art is an all new travel line that shows you where you are going and was path you are taking. Before it wasn't really clear what your driving path would look like and how long it takes you to get to your destination. With the new travel line it is much easier to see where you are going.

[h2]New pathfinding[/h2]

We implemented a new, smoother pathfinding system when driving around on the map with your hunters. Before you could only go in straight line from A to B. Now your vehicle will move smoothly along a nicely animated path. It looks better, feels better, and makes getting around the map way more satisfying.

[h2]Tons of new gameplay[/h2]

We also added a ton of new gameplay to the world map. Without giving too much away, you’ll now stumble upon rare locations and unexpected events—like the FBI chasing you down for all those shady break-ins. (What? Did you think stealing cash all the time had no consequences?)
Plus, gas management just got real. Run out of fuel, and you’ll find yourself stuck on the side of the road. Vehicles also have reworked stats, giving you more meaningful choices when building your hunting team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/c6dcad1d199d4865f71716e2509bc1e251d484ee.png[/img]
[i]Lots of choices in the vehicle selection screen now[/i]

[h2]Happy new 2025![/h2]

As usual Wayward Shadows is way behind schedule and far from completion but 2024 has been a great year nonetheless. I hope you all stick around for the great new stuff we have planned for 2025! As always, thank you for reading this and taking the time to keep up to date with development of Wayward Shadows!

Have a happy new year and a great 2025!

notes.title: Combat UI Updates
notes.content:
[h1]The combat UI is getting better[/h1]

Hello hunters!
Combat in Wayward Shadows is a huge part of the gameplay. No case is truly solved until the monster is put down for good. I want the combat to feel as smooth as possible and having a great and easy to use UI is a big part of that.
Over the past couple of weeks lots of improvements have been made to the combat UI. Here are some of them:

[list]
[*] Improved icons for all action buttons
[*] All action buttons now have mappable shortcuts
[*] New bag mechanic to allow swapping of items during battle
[*] New highlighting states for buttons and UI sprites
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/25825af8a0890ec2f98dd62a42f4aaa19c5305ad.png[/img]

When a hunter in battle is selected the player is presented with all stats, action and other relevant information. This whole part of the UI has gotten a big overhaul and is much less confusing to understand now. In addition to a lot of new icons, there are new tooltips, better highlighting and functioning shortcuts (finally!)

[h2]Swapping items in combat[/h2]

One of the coolest newest features is the ability to swap items from the backpack. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/7871b53e7c2bc114017ce70f15d0365608f8114b.gif[/img]

This feature has been on the to-do list for a while and now finally made it into the game. The ability to swap the items in your hand with those from the backpack is a real game changer since you can now bring alternative equipment into combat.
Swapping items doesn't cost any action points can be done quickly by clicking on the backpack and just dragging the items to where you want them.
Large backpacks are hard to find but allow you to bring up to three extra items into battle.

[h2]More UI improvements are coming[/h2]

The work on a better and more readable UI is ongoing of course and I have a huge backlog of things I'd like to add. Wayward Shadows is a UI heavy game and there is so much still missing, so this won't be the last UI focused update. After all there are a lot of other big-ticket items left to do, such as localization, full controller support, etc.
Stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: New Gameplay Trailer
notes.content:
[h1]New Gameplay Trailer[/h1]

We finally have a new gameplay trailer ready. Whoo-hoo! So far we only had the short story/intro video on the page. And while that was a pretty cool little video, it didn't really provide much information about the gameplay.
The game is still a bit away from being called a proper Alpha version but at least now we have enough gameplay footage for a proper gameplay trailer. You can spot a lot of new case solving and deduction gameplay in the trailer, as well as some new battle environments.

2024 is going to be a great year and there will be a lot more cool features coming!
Thank you for your continued interest in Wayward Shadows! We really hope you like our new gameplay trailer!

notes.title: Feature Spring Cleaning
notes.content:
[h1]Feature Spring Cleaning[/h1]

It has been a while since the last update, but a lot of things happened! Feature and code cleanup, rework of some of the older game systems and other un-sexy stuff.
You won’t really notice much difference just looking at the game, but things are much more stable and fluid now. There are some things though which are quite visible, such as an overhaul of the case stories: 

[h2]Case Stories[/h2]

We really wanted the cases to feel more like the episode of a TV show having a better arc. This is why most cases are now divided into three chapters, each with individual challenges.
While the first chapter of a case might focus on identifying the victim and the cause of death, the second chapter might focus on how to find and kill a specific monster, and so on.
There have also been a lot of improvements to the case solving UI itself: There are now new highlights on the drag and drop slots, more UI feedback, new tooltips, etc. All this makes it a bit easier to keep an overview of the case story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/5eb2ec2e2b3839282d0dbde91a254a830af45f52.png[/img]

As you can see in the above screenshot, a case story now has three chapters, each new one unlocked when the previous one has been solved. This allows us to craft better stories without overloading the player right away.

[h2]Localization[/h2]

Localization is a big topic for us since we want to translate the game to as many languages as we can, and having a robust localization system is quite important. Wayward Shadows is very text heavy, and we are trying to manage text in such a way that we can easily update and maintain everything. We worked a lot on the localization code in the last couple weeks and now have a good system in place to set up and localize game strings. Not much to see or show though, since it all happens in the code.

[h2]Steam Page Face Lift[/h2]

And last but not least, the Steam page has gotten a little face lift with new gameplay screenshots, updated text, etc. There is still no proper gameplay trailer at the moment, but I am hoping we’ll have that ready soon.
Stay tuned! 2024 is going to have a lot of great progress and much more cool stuff to show.

notes.title: Battle, Buffs, and Throwables
notes.content:
[h1]Battle, Buffs, and Throwables[/h1]

I am still quite a bit away from putting together a decent trailer showcasing the gameplay in one nice clip but there has been a ton of progress over the last weeks.
The turn-based battle mode in particular got a lot of upgrades. I got the buffs/debuffs working and attacks can now buff/debuff units. A lot of cool stuff works now:

[list]
[*] Hunters and monsters can now get buffs/debuffs in battle that last X turns
[*] Hunters can get buffs buffs that last in battel and on the world map
[*] All equipment now supports on-use buffs debuffs
[*] World map actions, hustles skill-checks can now give buffs/debuffs
[*] Critical fail/success rolls from skill-check now give special new buffs.
[/list]

And you can now also throw grenades and other things! Currently I only got the flashbang and a normal grenade working but the code base is done and now it is just a matter of creating more assets and effects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/11f2bdf072f28a1ef7bbcd30dfa5d94174b1f73c.png[/img]

[h2]Damage Dice[/h2]
The damage dice also got a big upgrade and the damage type is now specific to the die and not the whole attack. Along with this the tooltips have been reworked and now show the exact amount of dice and the type of damage they do.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/5a0c38c16f2285be135dde1d51017b811e3375de.png[/img]

Now, monster AI and general behavior in the battle is still lacking but we are getting there. I hope I have some cool and functioning monster AI to show soon. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Small Town Living
notes.content:
[h3]Small Town Living[/h3]
The mysterious cases you will solve in Wayward Shadows take place in small towns all over the US. Each town is different, with a unique layout, buildings and environments.

Each town you enter will have lots of buildings and locations to discover. As the case develops and you find new clues, new locations will become available to explore. Obviously traveling between locations in the town is important, so a lot depends on what vehicle you have chosen for your run. Traveling in Wayward Shadows takes time, and the clock never stops, which means you have to think and plan ahead where and how often to travel. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/1ddcdba51df7c710045c6aa28f74a7ff4bae6dc0.png[/img]

In addition to locations which are relevant to your current case, each town always has a couple of basic buildings, such as a motel for you to rest and heal or a pawn shop to buy and sell equipment. And you can always hover over a building to get more information before driving to it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/a85b1e7a675bbbd2906a19cdb9c891c08f4f02dc.png[/img]

[h3]Look and Feel[/h3]
Getting the visuals and the tech right for those towns has been quite a challenge. The town generation algorithm and the accompanying art assets have all been through multiple reworks. 
I have tweaked the zooming and panning on the map a lot so that it feels better, but there is still plenty of work to be done.
Check out this screenshot of the current town map rendering taken from the latest dev build of the game vs an older version a couple months old.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/bab682f4135565b00b467bcb005fdc4e1fb95ac2.png[/img]

Thank you for reading! I hope you are all looking forward to finally get to play this game as much as I am having have fun building it!
Talk to you soon!

notes.title: Can You Solve The Case?
notes.content:
[h1]More than fighting[/h1]
Monster hunting is more than just fighting and killing dangerous monsters. Gathering clues and interviewing witnesses is a big part of solving cases. Knowing what monster you face in battle and what strengths and weaknesses it has is going to be vital for your survival. While the turn-based battles in Wayward shadows are a lot of fun, the cases leading up to them are quite important too.
You don't want to be unprepared and bring a wooden stake to a Werewolf fight!

Your most important tool for solving a case is your journal. This is where you keep all the clues and information for the monsters that you found. Check out the work-in-progress screenshot of the hunter journal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/39552338c685329aeac69f5f2bac3b37b25ce00f.png[/img]

[h1]Procedurally generated mysteries[/h1]
Each case you solve in Wayward Shadows is different. Not only will you be hunting different monsters, but the way to identifying and finding a dangerous monster requires a lot of detective work. Not wo cases are the same and each time you enter a new town to help out the people there, a new case is being generated with different challenges, clues and storylines.
Even after hours and hours of fighting evil, each case will feel new and fresh. 

[h1]Finding clues[/h1]
New clues can be obtained by talking to witnesses and convincing them to share information with you.
Once you meet a new character in the game you have the option to talk to them and get them to tell you more.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/d768f00dbe1d708799d8b906571d11a4c8b3b862.png[/img]

Check out the work-in-progress screenshot of the dialog interface above. Here the hunters just found an important witness hanging out a the local bar. 
The bottom of the location window shows a list of 'Location Action' buttons which allow you to interact with locations and people. What actions are available depends on the location, the people there, your hunting team and a lot of different things.

We are still working on the character conversations and interactions and hopefully have a bit more to show soon! There are a couple of pretty cool skill-check based mechanics that we can't wait to show.
Stay tuned!

notes.title: Items and Equipment
notes.content:
[h1]Items and Equipment[/h1]
A big part of the fun of going on a new journey in Wayward Shadows is to find and manage equipment, weapons and armor to help you in your fight against the forces of evil.
New items can be found in certain locations while you are working a case or, if you are lucky, you can buy useful things at the local pawn shop,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/265cdcb14dccc87b313e346c887e212ce2a5c35c.png[/img]


[h2]Limited Capacity[/h2]
You can’t bring everything, and space is always limited. Each hunter can carry two weapons, one piece of armor and a backpack. You have more space to store things in the trunk of your vehicle but only the equipment in your hunter’s inventory will be available during battle. Better make sure to pack your silver items before you face a Werewolf!
And last month I finally finished work on the new backpack system which now allows you to use and manage bag items to gain more space. A simple looking feature but it was pretty tricky to implement. Once a bag is equipped it opens up additional storage slots for your hunter.
Having a large backpack that allows you to bring more items is super useful, but also very hard to find.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/f95b66f3ae5c567cda28b1fb81d9eb03be4a4b56.gif[/img]

[h2]Equipment Generation[/h2]
Weapons, armor and other equipment items are not randomly generated but set up manually and can then be found in the world. This means you will not encounter any items with random names and values but only hand-tweaked items. This makes sure each item will feel unique and well designed. 
There is a lot of code and balancing that takes care of the drop rates, availability, etc. but this part is still heavily work-in-progress. I am looking forward to the first playtests to see how this works and if players like it.
Stay tuned for more information. I am hard at work on adding more hunters, monsters and equipment and I hope I have to show more soon.
Thank you and have fun!

notes.title: How to build a hunting team
notes.content:
[h2] How to build a hunting team [/h2]

It’s dangerous to go alone! Better bring a partner when you go monster hunting.
At the start of every new run in Wayward Shadows you’ll first have to build your hunting team. That means picking two hunters and a vehicle to travel with. Once you have made your choice and started your run, this is it. You can not change your hunters or vehicle once you are on the road. 

[h3]Pick Your Hunters[/h3]

There are 9 different hunters to choose from, all with different stats, skills and starting equipment. This allows for a lot of different team combinations to support your favorite playstyle.
Not all hunters will be available right from the start though and you have to unlock them by completing various challenging achievements.
Each hunter starts with one unique skill and one weapon. You can of course find better equipment and even learn new skills later, but this is what you start with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/781fe9388793ce1380a6da3be39ab249cd9dd5d6.png[/img]
[i] (The team selection screen) [/i]

[h3]Pick Your Vehicle[/h3]

Every hunting team needs transportation. Which of the six available vehicles you pick for your run determines how fast you will get to your next case, how much you can transport and how comfortable the ride is.
All those values play a role and depending on your playstyle you want to choose the right vehicle for your hunters. Just like hunters, most vehicles also need to be unlocked by completing achievements. And to make it more personal you can even name your vehicle!

[h3]Each Run is Different[/h3]

All the different combinations of hunters and vehicles make every run unique and challenging. A big part of the fun is figuring out what combos work best and in what way to level them.
Once you start solving cases and killing monsters you’ll get to level up your hunters and improve their equipment. Dual-wielding baseball bats? Extra bottles of holy water? It is up to you to build the best hunting team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42765680/55924f33c87de52fffbc7274b7608e4dd7acb342.png[/img]
[i] (Jing and Bronco are on the road!)[/i]

I’ll try and post more info on character stats, equipment and how the leveling works in future updates.

If you like what you see, and would like to support the game please consider adding it to your wishlist. Each wishlist addition goes a long way!
Thank you and have fun!
